transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I called EAP because I’ve been jumping really hard at little noises in the office—like a file drawer shutting or somebody dropping a coffee mug. My chest starts racing, and it takes way longer than it should to settle down.
Have you been through or witnessed something traumatic that still feels connected to these reactions?
Yeah. I remember him slamming the chair and standing in front of the door. But when I try to explain the worst part—the things he said—I just... blank out. It’s like that whole section got cut out.
Do unwanted memories of what happened ever suddenly pop into your mind?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed memories just popping into my head like that.
Do you go out of your way to avoid reminders of what happened?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding things because of it.
Do you often feel on guard or watchful, as if something bad could happen at any moment?
Yeah, especially at the office. I keep checking where my boss is, where the exits are, and whether someone’s coming up behind me, even when I’m supposed to be focused on my team.
Do you have nightmares about what happened?
No, I haven’t had any nightmares about it that I can remember.
Have you had sudden panic attacks that seemed to come out of nowhere, even when nothing was happening to remind you of what happened?
I’m not sure I’ve had anything like that. I haven’t noticed sudden panic attacks when nothing was going on.
Do you get especially anxious in situations where other people might judge, criticize, or watch you?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not really noticing anxiety just because people might be watching or judging me.
Since that incident, have you found yourself believing that people are dangerous or that nowhere is really safe?
No, I haven’t really started thinking people are dangerous or that nowhere is safe.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
No, not really. I worry about normal things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it spreading to a lot of different areas for no clear reason.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports exposure to a traumatic event, trauma-related hyperarousal with exaggerated startle and hypervigilance, autonomic reactivity, and dissociative inability to recall an important aspect of the trauma. Although intrusive memories, nightmares, and avoidance were denied, PTSD remains the best-fitting available diagnosis among the candidates because core trauma exposure plus arousal and dissociative trauma-related symptoms are present, and alternative anxiety presentations were not supported.
